claim: The TEAD reporter line shows Yap1 activity in vasculature, parachordal LECs (PLs) and cardinal vein sprouts at 2 dpf.
source: The TEAD reporter line [Tg(fli1:Gal4db-TEAD2ΔN-2A-mC);(UAS:GFP)] shows Yap1 activity in vasculature, parachordal LECs (PLs) and cardinal vein sprouts (arrowhead) of the 2 dpf trunk (A)
evidence: The claim is supported by Figure 1A showing TEAD reporter expression in the described tissues at 2 dpf.

claim: The TEAD reporter line shows Yap1 activity in the thoracic duct at 5 dpf.
source: The TEAD reporter line [Tg(fli1:Gal4db-TEAD2ΔN-2A-mC);(UAS:GFP)] shows Yap1 activity in vasculature, parachordal LECs (PLs) and cardinal vein sprouts (arrowhead) of the 2 dpf trunk (A) as well as in the thoracic duct (TD) at 5 dpf (B).
evidence: The claim is supported by Figure 1B showing TEAD reporter expression in the thoracic duct at 5 dpf.

claim: Expression was detected throughout the dorsal aorta (DA), the intersegmental vessels (ISVs) and PCV at 30 hpf, parachordal LEC progenitors (PLs, 2 dpf) and the thoracic duct at 5 dpf.
source: Expression was detected throughout the dorsal aorta (DA), the intersegmental vessels (ISVs) and PCV at 30 hpf, parachordal LEC progenitors (PLs, 2 dpf) and the thoracic duct at 5 dpf (Figure 1A,B, Video 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1A,B and Video 1 demonstrating TEAD reporter expression in the specified vascular structures at the indicated developmental stages.

claim: Nuclear EGFP-YAP in PL nuclei is highly variable between PLs within the same embryo relative to H2B-mCherry.
source: We found nuclear EGFP-YAP in PL nuclei that was highly variable between PLs within the same embryo (relative to H2B-mCherry), despite both proteins being driven from the fli1a promoter (Figure 1C–G).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 1C-G demonstrating variability in nuclear EGFP-YAP levels between PLs in the same embryo.

claim: Differences in the nuclear concentration of EGFP-YAP between PLs correlate with differences in the nuclear-cytoplasmic ratio of EGFP-YAP.
source: We found that differences in the nuclear concentration of EGFP-YAP between PLs (calculated as nuclear EGFP-YAP/mCherry) correlated with differences in the nuclear-cytoplasmic ratio of EGFP-YAP (Figure 1H and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 1H and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–C.

claim: EGFP-YAP did not change or fluctuate rapidly over short developmental time periods (imaged over 90 min of development).
source: Interestingly, when we measured nuclear EGFP-YAP intensities using high speed spinning disc microscopy, we found that EGFP-YAP did not change or fluctuate rapidly over short developmental time periods (imaged over 90 min of development) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F–F", Video 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by time-lapse imaging data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F–F" and Video 2.

claim: Quantification of nuclear EGFP-YAP levels in individual PLs over longer periods of development revealed dynamic changes.
source: However, quantification of nuclear EGFP-YAP levels in individual PLs over longer periods of development revealed dynamic changes (Video 3, Figure 1I, Figure 1—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: The claim is supported by time-lapse imaging and quantification data shown in Video 3, Figure 1I, and Figure 1—figure supplement 1G.

claim: Dynamic changes in nuclear EGFP-YAP were not associated simply with breakdown of the nuclear lamina during cell division.
source: Detailed cell tracking analyses showed that these changes were not associated simply with breakdown of the nuclear lamina during cell division (Figure 1I (arrow in cell track two indicates a cell division), Figure 1—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: The claim is supported by cell tracking data shown in Figure 1I and Figure 1—figure supplement 1G.

claim: YAP is dynamically regulated in PLs during lymphatic development.
source: Taken together, these observations suggest that YAP is dynamically regulated in PLs during lymphatic development.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation of dynamic changes in nuclear EGFP-YAP levels over developmental time that are not associated with cell division.

claim: Zyap1-/- mutants show only subtle lymphatic defects with a minor reduction in thoracic duct formation.
source: Using transgenic lines to visualise developing veins and lymphatics (TgBAC(dab2b:EGFP)ncv67, Tg(kdrl:mCherry)ncv502), we observed only subtle lymphatic defects in Zyap1ncv101-/- mutants with a minor reduction in thoracic duct formation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,C.

claim: MZyap1-/- mutants failed to form a mature trunk lymphatic vasculature.
source: Strikingly, while the overall morphology of MZyap1-/- mutants at 5 dpf appeared relatively normal with mutant embryos displaying subtle craniofacial defects and a missing swim bladder (Figure 2A), MZyap1-/- mutants failed to form a mature trunk lymphatic vasculature (Figure 2B–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2A-E demonstrating absence of trunk lymphatic vasculature in MZyap1-/- mutants.

claim: The craniofacial lymphatic network had developed normally in MZyap1-/- mutants.
source: However, the craniofacial lymphatic network had developed normally (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B, D)
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B, D.

claim: Blood flow remained intact and functional with apparently normal morphology of blood vessels in the 5 dpf trunk in MZyap1-/- mutants.
source: and blood flow remained intact and functional with apparently normal morphology of blood vessels in the 5 dpf trunk (Figure 2B–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2B-C.

claim: MZyap1-/- mutants had a transient, mild reduction in the number of EC nuclei in intersegmental vessel (ISV) sprouts at 24 hpf.
source: Compared with wildtype siblings, MZyap1-/- mutants had a transient, mild reduction in the number of EC nuclei in intersegmental vessel (ISV) sprouts (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A,D,E), prominent in the most posterior sprouts analysed (Figure 2—figure supplement 2F) at 24 hpf.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A,D,E,F.

claim: The number of ECs in each vessel had largely recovered by 32 hpf in MZyap1-/- mutants.
source: However, the number of ECs in each vessel had largely recovered by 32 hpf (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B,D,E,F).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B,D,E,F.

claim: Yap1 is necessary to form a lymphatic vasculature, but not blood vasculature.
source: The above observations indicate that yap1 is necessary to form a lymphatic vasculature, but not blood vasculature.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that MZyap1-/- mutants lack trunk lymphatic vasculature but have normal blood vasculature.

claim: MZyap1-/- mutant ECs were able to form arterial grafts at frequencies comparable to wildtype EC grafts.
source: Across n = 24 mutant EC grafts, MZyap1-/- mutant ECs were able to form arterial grafts at frequencies comparable to wildtype EC grafts.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data from transplantation experiments shown in Figure 2I.

claim: MZyap1-/- mutant ECs formed venous grafts at a slightly reduced frequency.
source: However, MZyap1-/- mutant ECs formed venous grafts at a slightly reduced frequency
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data from transplantation experiments shown in Figure 2I.

claim: MZyap1-/- mutant ECs failed to contribute to lymphatic vessels except for small numbers of cells in just n = 2/24 transplanted embryos.
source: and failed to contribute to lymphatic vessels except for small numbers of cells in just n = 2/24 transplanted embryos (compared with n = 10/23 robust contributions in embryos transplanted with WT cells) (Figure 2G–I).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data from transplantation experiments shown in Figure 2G-I.

claim: Yap1 has a cell autonomous role in trunk lymphangiogenesis.
source: Overall, this indicates that Yap1 has a cell autonomous role in trunk lymphangiogenesis.
evidence: The claim is inferred from transplantation experiments showing that MZyap1-/- mutant ECs fail to contribute to lymphatic vessels in wildtype hosts.

claim: MZyap1-/- mutants show a reduction in the total number of ECs sprouting from the PCV at 2 dpf.
source: We scored MZyap1-/- mutants for ECs sprouting from the PCV at 2 dpf and found a reduction in the total number of ECs departing the vein (Figure 3A–B).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 3A-B.

claim: MZyap1-/- mutants show almost a complete loss of PLs, but near normal numbers of ECs in venous intersegmental blood vessels.
source: Strikingly, we saw almost a complete loss of PLs, but near normal numbers of ECs in venous intersegmental blood vessels (Figure 3A,C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 3A,C,D.

claim: By 3 dpf, PL numbers in the HM remained reduced but showed recovery compared with sibling controls in MZyap1-/- mutants.
source: By 3 dpf, PL numbers in the HM remained reduced but showed recovery compared with sibling controls (Figure 3E).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Prox1 expression in the PCV and LECs departing the PCV was unchanged at 36 hpf in MZyap1-/- mutants.
source: We found that Prox1 expression in the PCV and LECs departing the PCV was unchanged at 36 hpf (Figure 3F,G).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3F,G.

claim: Yap1 is not required for the induction of lymphatic identity but is needed to establish normal numbers of LECs in sprouts arising from the PCV.
source: Thus, Yap1 is not required for the induction of lymphatic identity but is needed to establish normal numbers of LECs in sprouts arising from the PCV.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Prox1 expression is normal but PL numbers are reduced in MZyap1-/- mutants.

claim: MZyap1-/- mutants exhibit abnormal behaviours of sprouts arising from the PCV, most commonly sprouts appeared thickened, retracted, or turned ventrally and formed abnormal loops.
source: We observed striking abnormal behaviours of sprouts arising from the PCV in MZyap1-/- mutants, most commonly sprouts appeared thickened, retracted, or turned ventrally and formed abnormal loops (Video 5, mutant 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by time-lapse imaging data shown in Video 5 and Figure 3H.

claim: Venous sprouts in MZyap1-/- mutants often formed abnormal connections with other venous sprouts from adjacent body segments.
source: Often venous sprouts formed abnormal connections with other venous sprouts from adjacent body segments (Video 6, mutant 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by time-lapse imaging data shown in Video 6 and Figure 3H.

claim: Abnormal behaviours and reduced sprouting cell numbers likely contribute to fewer PLs accurately seeding the HM during development.
source: These abnormal behaviours and reduced sprouting cell numbers likely contribute to fewer PLs accurately seeding the HM during development.
evidence: The claim is speculative, inferring a causal relationship between observed abnormal sprouting behaviors and reduced PL numbers.

claim: The effect of Vegfc stimulation on EC proliferation was completely blocked upon yap1 MO injection but not upon p53 (control) MO injection.
source: The effect of Vegfc stimulation was completely blocked upon yap1 MO injection but not upon p53 (control) MO injection (Figure 4B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 4B,C.

claim: Yap1 functions downstream of Vegfc in Vegfc-induced proliferation.
source: Together, these observations are consistent with a role for Yap1 downstream of Vegfc, functioning in Vegfc-induced proliferation.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that yap1 knockdown blocks Vegfc-induced EC proliferation.

claim: MZyap1-/- mutant host embryos displayed a vast reduction (although not a complete block) in numbers of proliferative PLs adjacent to HM grafts compared with wildtype siblings.
source: Strikingly, the MZyap1-/- mutant host embryos displayed a vast reduction (although not a complete block) in numbers of proliferative PLs adjacent to HM grafts compared with wildtype siblings (Figure 4F,G).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data from transplantation experiments shown in Figure 4F,G.

claim: Yap1 plays a role in the proliferation of developing lymphatic progenitors stimulated by Vegfc.
source: These data, coupled with reduced numbers of ECs in sprouts departing the PCV (Figure 3B), together suggest that Yap1 plays a role in the proliferation of developing lymphatic progenitors stimulated by Vegfc.
evidence: The claim is inferred from multiple lines of evidence including reduced EC numbers in sprouts and reduced response to Vegfc-induced proliferation in yap1 mutants.

claim: Vegfc responsive PLs displayed an increase in nuclear EGFP-YAP compared with control PLs.
source: We found that Vegfc responsive PLs displayed an increase in nuclear EGFP-YAP compared with control PLs (Figure 5C',D).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data from transplantation experiments shown in Figure 5C',D.

claim: The increase in nuclear EGFP-YAP in the vegfc-OE transplanted embryos was concomitant with a higher number of PLs.
source: This increase in nuclear EGFP-YAP in the vegfc-OE transplanted embryos was concomitant with a higher number of PLs (Figure 5G).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: EGFP-YAP was increased in nuclei in lymphatic and venous EC grafts in the vegfc-OE hosts relative to nuclear concentration in grafted vegfc-unresponsive DA cells.
source: Relative to nuclear concentration in grafted vegfc-unresponsive DA cells, EGFP-YAP was increased in nuclei in lymphatic and venous EC grafts in the vegfc-OE hosts (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data from transplantation experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B–E.

claim: Treatment with SL327, a MEK inhibitor that blocks Erk signalling in zebrafish, decreased the concentration of EGFP-YAP in the nuclei of PLs, concomitant with a reduction in PL number.
source: Treatment with SL327, a MEK inhibitor that blocks Erk signalling in zebrafish (Shin et al., 2016), decreased the concentration of EGFP-YAP in the nuclei of PLs, concomitant with a reduction in PL number (Figure 5E,H–J).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data from drug treatment experiments shown in Figure 5E,H–J and cites previous work on SL327.

claim: The Vegfc-Erk axis promotes high nuclear Yap1 and drives normal sprouting and proliferation during zebrafish developmental lymphangiogenesis.
source: Overall, these observations indicate that the Vegfc-Erk axis promotes high nuclear Yap1 and drives normal sprouting and proliferation during zebrafish developmental lymphangiogenesis.
evidence: The claim is inferred from multiple lines of evidence including Vegfc-induced increase in nuclear YAP and Erk inhibition reducing nuclear YAP.

claim: Loss of Yap1 has a dramatic effect upon lymphatic vascular development, as MZyap1-/- mutants fail to form a lymphatic network in the zebrafish trunk.
source: We show here that loss of Yap1 has a dramatic effect upon lymphatic vascular development, as MZyap1-/- mutants fail to form a lymphatic network in the zebrafish trunk.
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2B-E.

claim: MZyap1-/- mutants exhibit a largely normal blood vasculature.
source: Surprisingly, these mutants exhibit a largely normal blood vasculature.
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2B-C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The severity of the MZyap1-/- mutant phenotype indicates that Yap1 is indispensable for lymphangiogenesis and its paralogue Taz is not able to fully compensate in lymphatic vasculature.
source: The severity of the MZyap1-/- mutant phenotype indicates that Yap1 is indispensable for lymphangiogenesis and its paralogue Taz is not able to fully compensate in lymphatic vasculature.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the severe lymphatic phenotype in MZyap1-/- mutants.

claim: Lymphatic endothelial progenitor cells are specified in MZyap1-/- mutants but these fail to sprout normally to the horizontal myoseptum.
source: Lymphatic endothelial progenitor cells are specified in MZyap1-/- mutants but these fail to sprout normally to the horizontal myoseptum.
evidence: The claim is supported by data showing normal Prox1 expression (Figure 3F,G) but abnormal sprouting behaviors (Figure 3H, Videos 5-6).

claim: YAP and TAZ play important roles in vasculature.
source: Recent studies have demonstrated that YAP and TAZ play important roles in vasculature (Kim et al., 2017; Neto et al., 2018; Wang et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Yap knockout mice are lethal due to developmental arrest of the embryo and severe defects in the yolk sac vasculature.
source: While Yap knockout mice are lethal due to developmental arrest of the embryo and severe defects in the yolk sac vasculature (Morin-Kensicki et al., 2006)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Endothelial specific deletion of Yap and Taz leads to vascular defects due to impaired EC sprouting and proliferation.
source: endothelial specific deletion of Yap and Taz leads to vascular defects due to impaired EC sprouting and proliferation (Kim et al., 2017; Neto et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Nuclear YAP/TAZ promotes proliferation and cell survival while retention of YAP/TAZ in the cytoplasm leads to apoptosis in endothelial cells.
source: In endothelial cells (ECs), nuclear YAP/TAZ promotes proliferation and cell survival while retention of YAP/TAZ in the cytoplasm leads to apoptosis (Panciera et al., 2017; Zhao et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: YAP/TAZ in blood vascular ECs regulate angiogenesis downstream of VEGFA both by modulating cellular proliferation and controlling adherens junctional dynamics during vessel morphogenesis.
source: Moreover, it has been suggested that YAP/TAZ in blood vascular ECs regulate angiogenesis downstream of VEGFA both by modulating cellular proliferation and controlling adherens junctional dynamics during vessel morphogenesis (Neto et al., 2018; Wang et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Roles for Yap and Taz have been recently shown in lymphatic vessel morphogenesis in development and postnatal settings in mice, but the mechanisms of action remain to be fully appreciated.
source: Roles for Yap and Taz have been recently shown in lymphatic vessel morphogenesis in development and postnatal settings in mice, but the mechanisms of action remain to be fully appreciated (Cho et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work and acknowledges gaps in understanding.

claim: YAP has been found to respond to altered flow patterns in zebrafish and in cultured blood and lymphatic ECs.
source: YAP has further been found to respond to altered flow patterns in zebrafish and in cultured blood and lymphatic ECs (Nakajima et al., 2017; Sabine et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Yap1 contributes to blood vessel maintenance in zebrafish, although blood vessels still undergo normal angiogenesis in zebrafish yap1 mutant models.
source: Yap1 also contributes to blood vessel maintenance in zebrafish, although blood vessels still undergo normal angiogenesis in zebrafish yap1 mutant models (Nakajima et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Yap1 is indispensable for lymphatic vascular development.
source: Here we utilise zebrafish mutants and live imaging of zebrafish reporters of YAP activity to show that Yap1 is indispensable for lymphatic vascular development.
evidence: The claim is supported by data from yap1 mutant analysis showing failure to form trunk lymphatic vasculature.

claim: Yap1 acts in a cell autonomous manner and is necessary at stages of lymphangiogenesis driven by Vegfc/Flt4 signalling.
source: Yap1 acts in a cell autonomous manner and is necessary at stages of lymphangiogenesis driven by Vegfc/Flt4 signalling.
evidence: The claim is supported by transplantation experiments (Figure 2F-I) and Vegfc overexpression experiments (Figure 4).

claim: Unlike mutants in the Vegfc/Flt4 pathway, Yap1 mutants display normal specification of Prox1-positive lymphatic progenitors coincident with aberrant cellular behaviours during LEC sprouting.
source: However, unlike mutants in the Vegfc/Flt4 pathway Yap1 mutants display normal specification of Prox1-positive lymphatic progenitors coincident with aberrant cellular behaviours during LEC sprouting.
evidence: The claim is supported by data showing normal Prox1 expression (Figure 3F,G) but abnormal sprouting (Figure 3H, Videos 5-6).

claim: Yap1 is essential for Vegfc-induced EC proliferation.
source: We identify a central role for Yap1 in Vegfc-induced EC proliferation
evidence: The claim is supported by data from Vegfc overexpression experiments with yap1 knockdown (Figure 4) and transplantation experiments (Figure 4D-G).

claim: The nuclear concentration of YAP changes dynamically in lymphatic progenitors, driven by Vegfc.
source: and show that the nuclear concentration of YAP changes dynamically in lymphatic progenitors, driven by Vegfc.
evidence: The claim is supported by data showing increased nuclear YAP in response to Vegfc (Figure 5) and decreased nuclear YAP with Erk inhibition (Figure 5E,H-J).

claim: Paracrine Vegfc-signalling ultimately increases nuclear YAP in lymphatic progenitors to control lymphatic development.
source: Paracrine Vegfc-signalling ultimately increases nuclear YAP in lymphatic progenitors to control lymphatic development.
evidence: The claim is supported by data from transplantation experiments showing increased nuclear YAP in PLs adjacent to Vegfc-producing cells (Figure 5).

claim: During embryonic development, the lymphatic vascular network derives chiefly from pre-existing veins.
source: During embryonic development, the lymphatic vascular network derives chiefly from pre-existing veins.
evidence: The claim represents established scientific knowledge about lymphatic development.

claim: In the E9-9.5 mouse embryo, complex, multicellular lymphatic vessels are ultimately generated from a limited pool of lymphatic endothelial cell (LEC) progenitors first specified along the cardinal veins.
source: In the E9-9.5 mouse embryo, complex, multicellular lymphatic vessels are ultimately generated from a limited pool of lymphatic endothelial cell (LEC) progenitors first specified along the cardinal veins (Oliver and Srinivasan, 2010; Wigle and Oliver, 1999).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: LEC progenitors sprout and progressively colonise embryonic tissues over developmental time.
source: LEC progenitors sprout and progressively colonise embryonic tissues over developmental time (Hägerling et al., 2013; Koltowska et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: In the zebrafish trunk, a complex lymphatic vasculature is established within just a few days and from a very limited number of progenitors.
source: In the zebrafish trunk, a complex lymphatic vasculature is established within just a few days and from a very limited number of progenitors (Koltowska et al., 2015a; Nicenboim et al., 2015; Shin et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Beginning from around 32–34 hr post fertilisation (hpf), lymphangiogenesis generates a functional lymphatic network by 5 days post fertilisation (dpf).
source: Beginning from around 32–34 hr post fertilisation (hpf), lymphangiogenesis generates a functional lymphatic network by 5 days post fertilisation (dpf) (Hogan and Schulte-Merker, 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Prox1 is a transcription factor that is essential for development of LECs in both mice and zebrafish.
source: Precursor cells in the cardinal vein obtain lymphatic identity upon induction of Prox1 expression, a transcription factor that is essential for development of LECs in both mice and zebrafish (Johnson et al., 2008; Koltowska et al., 2015a; Wigle and Oliver, 1999).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Sprouting of LECs from the cardinal veins is governed by Vegfc signalling acting through the endothelial receptor Vegfr3 (Flt4) in both mice and zebrafish.
source: Sprouting of LECs from the cardinal veins is governed by Vegfc signalling acting through the endothelial receptor Vegfr3 (Flt4) in both mice and zebrafish (Hogan et al., 2009b; Karkkainen et al., 2004; Le Guen et al., 2014; Veikkola et al., 2001; Villefranc et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Zebrafish Vegfc and Vegfd play partially compensatory roles in both trunk and craniofacial lymphangiogenesis.
source: Zebrafish Vegfc and Vegfd also play partially compensatory roles in both trunk and craniofacial lymphangiogenesis (Astin et al., 2014; Bower et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Mutations in VEGFC and VEGFR3 cause primary lymphedema in humans.
source: Underlining the conservation of this pathway in lymphangiogenesis, mutations in VEGFC and VEGFR3 cause primary lymphedema in humans (Gordon et al., 2013; Irrthum et al., 2000; Karkkainen et al., 2000).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Induction of Vegfr3 signalling in LECs by Vegfc triggers the activation of multiple downstream intracellular signalling events involved in cell migration, survival and cellular proliferation.
source: Ultimately, induction of Vegfr3 signalling in LECs by Vegfc triggers the activation of multiple downstream intracellular signalling events involved in cell migration, survival and cellular proliferation (Deng et al., 2015; Zheng et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: In the zebrafish, Vegfc-Flt4 signalling acts to induce Prox1 expression at the earliest stages of lymphatic specification.
source: In the zebrafish, Vegfc-Flt4 signalling acts to induce Prox1 expression at the earliest stages of lymphatic specification (Koltowska et al., 2015a; Shin et al., 2016)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: A role for Vegfc-Flt4 signalling in specification remains to be fully explored in the mouse model.
source: although a role in specification remains to be fully explored in the mouse model.
evidence: The claim acknowledges a gap in current knowledge.

claim: The Hippo pathway and effector transcription factors, YAP and TAZ, are key regulators of normal and pathological organ and tissue growth.
source: Key regulators of normal and pathological organ and tissue growth are the Hippo pathway and effector transcription factors, YAP and TAZ, which have been shown to promote proliferation, suppress apoptosis and modulate cellular and tissue morphogenesis (Harvey et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: YAP and TAZ have been shown to promote proliferation, suppress apoptosis and modulate cellular and tissue morphogenesis.
source: Key regulators of normal and pathological organ and tissue growth are the Hippo pathway and effector transcription factors, YAP and TAZ, which have been shown to promote proliferation, suppress apoptosis and modulate cellular and tissue morphogenesis (Harvey et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: YAP and TAZ drive target gene expression by binding to the TEAD1-4 transcriptional co-factors.
source: YAP and its paralogue TAZ are transcriptional co-factors that drive target gene expression by binding to the TEAD1-4 transcriptional co-factors (Pobbati and Hong, 2013; Yu and Guan, 2013; Yu et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: YAP and TAZ have been implicated as oncogenes that are commonly upregulated in various cancer types including colon and breast cancer.
source: As potent drivers of cell proliferation, YAP and TAZ have been implicated as oncogenes that are commonly upregulated in various cancer types including colon and breast cancer (Harvey et al., 2013; Varelas, 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The classical HIPPO pathway inhibits YAP/TAZ signalling by retaining the effectors in the cytoplasm through the activation of a phosphorylation cascade.
source: The classical HIPPO pathway inhibits YAP/TAZ signalling by retaining the effectors in the cytoplasm through the activation of a phosphorylation cascade.
evidence: The claim represents established knowledge about the Hippo pathway mechanism.

claim: The kinase MST1/2 phosphorylates another kinase LATS1/2, which subsequently phosphorylates YAP/TAZ.
source: The kinase MST1/2 phosphorylates another kinase LATS1/2, which subsequently phosphorylates YAP/TAZ.
evidence: The claim represents established knowledge about the Hippo pathway mechanism.

claim: Phosphorylation of YAP/TAZ sequesters YAP/TAZ in the cytoplasm and leads to their degradation.
source: This phosphorylation sequesters YAP/TAZ in the cytoplasm and leads to their degradation (Yu and Guan, 2013; Yu et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: YAP and TAZ function in the cytoplasm, at cell-cell junctions and in the nucleus as core integrators of extracellular stimuli such as growth factor signalling, mechanical forces and cellular adhesion.
source: Ultimately, YAP and TAZ function in the cytoplasm, at cell-cell junctions and in the nucleus as core integrators of extracellular stimuli such as growth factor signalling, mechanical forces and cellular adhesion (Panciera et al., 2017; Varelas, 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: YAP displays dynamic changes in lymphatic progenitors.
source: Here we show that YAP displays dynamic changes in lymphatic progenitors
evidence: The claim is supported by data showing dynamic changes in nuclear EGFP-YAP over developmental time (Figure 1I, Figure 1—figure supplement 1G, Video 3).

claim: Maternal and Zygotic (MZ) yap1 mutants show normal specification of lymphatic progenitors.
source: Maternal and Zygotic (MZ) yap1 mutants show normal specification of lymphatic progenitors, abnormal cellular sprouting and reduced numbers of lymphatic progenitors emerging from the cardinal vein during lymphangiogenesis.
evidence: The claim is supported by data showing normal Prox1 expression in MZyap1-/- mutants (Figure 3F,G).

claim: Maternal and Zygotic (MZ) yap1 mutants show abnormal cellular sprouting.
source: Maternal and Zygotic (MZ) yap1 mutants show normal specification of lymphatic progenitors, abnormal cellular sprouting and reduced numbers of lymphatic progenitors emerging from the cardinal vein during lymphangiogenesis.
evidence: The claim is supported by time-lapse imaging data showing abnormal sprouting behaviors (Figure 3H, Videos 5-6).

claim: Maternal and Zygotic (MZ) yap1 mutants show reduced numbers of lymphatic progenitors emerging from the cardinal vein during lymphangiogenesis.
source: Maternal and Zygotic (MZ) yap1 mutants show normal specification of lymphatic progenitors, abnormal cellular sprouting and reduced numbers of lymphatic progenitors emerging from the cardinal vein during lymphangiogenesis.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data showing reduced numbers of ECs departing the PCV (Figure 3A-B).

claim: Yap1 is indispensable for Vegfc-induced proliferation in a transgenic model of Vegfc overexpression.
source: Furthermore, Yap1 is indispensable for Vegfc-induced proliferation in a transgenic model of Vegfc overexpression.
evidence: The claim is supported by data showing that yap1 knockdown blocks Vegfc-induced EC proliferation (Figure 4B,C) and that MZyap1-/- mutants show reduced response to Vegfc-producing grafts (Figure 4D-G).

claim: This work suggests a dynamic signalling mechanism integrating Vegfc/Flt4 signalling with Yap1 control of LEC proliferation and cellular behaviour during trunk lymphatic vascular development.
source: This work suggests a dynamic signalling mechanism integrating Vegfc/Flt4 signalling with Yap1 control of LEC proliferation and cellular behaviour during trunk lymphatic vascular development.
evidence: The claim is inferred from multiple lines of evidence showing Vegfc-induced increase in nuclear YAP, Yap1 requirement for Vegfc-induced proliferation, and Yap1 requirement for normal sprouting.

claim: The yap1ncv101-/- mutant has a 25 bp deletion in exon1 leading to a frame shift and stop codon after 71 bp, prior to the TEAD binding domain.
source: We analysed two different mutant strains: yap1ncv101-/- mutants have a 25 bp deletion in exon1 leading to a frame shift and stop codon after 71 bp, prior to the TEAD binding domain (Nakajima et al., 2017)
evidence: The claim describes the molecular nature of the yap1ncv101 allele and is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The yap1mw48-/- mutant displays a 4 bp deletion after 158 bp, truncating the TEAD binding domain and leading to a premature stop codon.
source: and yap1mw48-/- mutants display a 4 bp deletion after 158 bp, truncating the TEAD binding domain and leading to a premature stop codon (Miesfeld et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim describes the molecular nature of the yap1mw48 allele and is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Analysis of the two yap1 alleles revealed equivalent phenotypes.
source: Analysis of the two alleles revealed equivalent phenotypes.
evidence: The claim is supported by data showing similar lymphatic phenotypes in both yap1ncv101-/- and yap1mw48-/- mutants (Figure 2, Figure 3).
